oeis-a084611.reason: Kotěšovec's 3-page web note gets the right value but is heuristic, not a proof. The key step, that the largest coefficient sits at p = n, is justified only by a plot, and the lower bound uses P_n(1/√5)^(1/n) → 1 although P_n(cos x) oscillates through zero. (The statement itself looks easy: by Parseval and Cauchy-Schwarz a(n)^(1/n) has the same limit as the L^{2n} norm of |1+z-z²| on |z|=1, whose max is √5. But the cited URL does not give that argument.)

oeis-a045406.reason: arXiv:2605.11351 proves Mathar's recurrence for a different sequence, A001711, not A045406. The two are related by a(n) = (−1)^n·4·A001711(n−6) = (−1)^n (n−3)!(2H_{n−3} − 3), which turns one recurrence into the other for n ≥ 8, but the paper does not state or prove that identity, and n = 5, 6, 7 need separate checks. (With that identity, which follows from differentiating the falling factorial, the site's statement is easy to prove here.)

mo-59886.reason: arXiv:0801.0059 (Peled-Yadin-Yehudayoff) bounds only the maximal probability that k-wise independent bits are all 1. That shows Gaussian-tail concentration can fail for linear statistics under small k (already the trivial point in the existing answer). It neither gives nor rules out a Talagrand-type concentration inequality for convex 1-Lipschitz F under k-wise independence with k-dependent bounds, which is what the question asks.

Erdos448.erdos_448.variants.erdos_tenenb.reason: Erdos-Tenenbaum 1981 (the link), Theorem 1, proves only the upper half: the upper density of {tau+(n) < a tau(n)} is <= c(eps) a^{1-eps}, i.e. liminf of log(upper density)/log a >= 1. The matching lower bound (upper density >= a^{1+o(1)}) is not in this paper. It comes from Hall-Tenenbaum, Divisors (1988) Ch. 4, quoted as (15) in Tenenbaum's 2013 survey, which would settle the statement.

mo-415983.reason: The link is McMullen's Upper Bound Theorem (Mathematika 1970) for general d-polytopes. Applied to sections with at most 2n facets it only gives a generic upper bound that ignores the diagonal constraint. It does not determine the maximal number of vertices of the cube section asked for, and the paper does not address cube sections.

oeis-a039827.reason: Almkvist (JNT 32, 1989) proves unimodality of products of (1-q^{rk})/(1-q^k), including prod (1+q^i+q^{2i}). Unimodality does not determine the number of distinct coefficient values (which needs strict increase apart from exactly two repeats on the half-range), so it does not give a(n) = n(n+1)/2 - 1, the recurrence or the g.f.
